title: Tricks and tchotchkes for AWS re:Invent
summary: Preparing for AWS re:Invent 2026? Explore firsthand tips for networking, planning meetings, finding the right sessions, and surviving a busy week in Vegas.
body_markdown:
We’re less than a month away from[re:Invent 2026](https://aws.amazon.com/events/reinvent/) , which means it’s time for my annual “Tips and tricks” list. Last year was my first year attending as an AWS outsider, so I included a few new perspectives (at the bottom). As always, please feel free to comment or send me any of your own suggestions.


There's always something new at AWS re:Invent, and fortunately the structure and flow of the event is similar each year, so whether this is your first re:Invent or your eleventh, here are a few ways to make the most of the week.


1. **Have a plan.** The amount of activity and opportunity to network at re:Invent is overwhelming. The Expo Hall is always buzzing, and it’s fun to peruse the aisles on swag hunts – and I always recommend connecting with new people and potential partners. Since there is so much content, it’s a good idea to establish the goals you want to accomplish and make a plan for each day – reserving some time for targeted networking, establishing new leads, and “unstructured socialization.” Without that plan, you’ll end the week with a stack of cards, but no measurable outcomes.
2. **Make time for the content.** Typically, technical attendees will prioritize attending sessions to learn about services, announcements, best practices, etc… but sales/partner attendees will focus solely on networking and side meetings. To the latter group, I recommend reserving time to take advantage of some of the session content – much of which can be really valuable and relevant. Yes, you can catch it afterwards on recording, but be honest… Will you? There’s always something special about seeing it in person – plus, there are networking opportunities in the sessions too (people of similar interests will be there).
3. **Give yourself time between meetings/sessions.** re:Invent is HUGE. Nothing is close… and the crowds may not move at the pace you need. Give yourself time… no need to create artificial stress for yourself (I give this advice knowing full well that I will likely not do well at this, myself). Getting around Vegas is intentionally confusing… The casinos’ plan for you to get so lost that you just give up and settle in at a Blackjack table. I’ve been to meetings in Bouchon every year and still have no idea how to get there (or how to get back from there).
4. **Document action items and schedule follow up meetings:** So many meetings, introductions, discussions, learnings… It’s impossible to keep track. Make sure to clearly document action items and schedule follow up meetings/discussions following re:Invent. If you say you’ll connect again after re:Invent without actually putting something on the calendar, it’ll likely get forgotten in the deluge of everything else. Optimally, your organization will have a system to centralize leads, communications, and follow ups... I've been thinking about such a system and did some ideating by creating a[Pega Blueprint](https://www.pega.com/blueprint) for it. If you'd like to see it, you can download it[here](https://dankasun-public-shares.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/Pega+GenAI+Blueprint+-+reInvent+Lead+Management+and+Follow+up+System.pdf) .
5. **Don’t try to do it all:** One of my favorite 80s songs is “Life in One Day” by Howard Jones. Basically, the message is: Pace yourself, if you try to do everything you’ll get overwhelmed and won’t enjoy it or accomplish anything (plus something about playing the flute…). Believe it or not, there is life after re:Invent. It is possible to meet someone at a later date (in person, Zoom, you name it). Sometimes it’s actually better to connect afterwards when everyone is more focused.
6. **Stay healthy:** re:Invent can be exhausting… with big crowds and lots of handshakes, often coupled with irregular meals and tendencies to overindulge (it is Vegas, after all). While you can’t get around that all completely without just staying in your room (which would be pointless), I recommend being mindful about it. Get as much sleep as you can, pace yourself, wash hands, and just be smart (and refer to the prior point). Staying healthy through the rest of the holidays would be a nice thing.
7. **There are TWO Grand Luxe Cafes… one in Venetian, one in Palazzo:** I fall for this EVERY YEAR. “Meet at the Grand Luxe” and, invariably, I end up at the wrong one (as do many others in our parties). They are **NOT** close… so if you pick wrong, you blow 20 valuable meeting-time minutes. Always double check (I will do so this year… I promise).
8. **Wear comfortable shoes:** You WILL be walking. A LOT. Make it easy on yourself… re:Invent isn’t the place where people question fashion choices 😊.
9. **Hydrate:** It's Vegas. It's dry... but you'll be so busy that it's easy to forget basic sustenance.
10. **Network, network, network:** re:Invent can be a social nightmare for those of us who are introverts (and yes, I meant "us") but we can't ignore the value of making new connections. If there's a time and place to step out of our comfort zone, re:Invent is it. Try not to be shy about introducing yourself and going out of your way to extend your network (borrowed from[Barb Huelskamp](https://www.linkedin.com/in/barb-huelskamp/) ). The good news: It's a tech conference, so we awkward introverts are likely the majority... so there's lots of good company to commiserate.
11. **Plan for ad-hoc side meetings:** Sounds counterintuitive but make sure to schedule in time for meetings that you haven't scheduled. There will be many instances where you'll make a valuable connection that needs further discussion – but if your schedule is already completely packed, you won't have time. Adding some margin for flexibility in your schedule can help make sure you don't miss these opportunities... and sometimes having "walking meetings" is a great (and only) way to do this (i.e., "I'm on my way over to a meeting at the Wynn, have 15 minutes to walk with me so we can discuss it?" - good tip borrowed from[Dr. James Mitchell](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jamesmitchellstrategicblue/) ).


## 2025 observation: A tale of two cities in Vegas


Attending from outside AWS wasn’t significantly different (I actually got to go into the keynote for a change – so that was new), but the outside view brought clarity to a few observations. The most notable observation: how distinct the attendee audiences can be throughout the event.


There are two worlds at re:Invent:


1. The tech folks who are catching up on the latest AWS services and announcements and learning more about complementing solutions from other vendors. They will be the most absorbed by the sessions and will dominate the traffic throughout the expo. They’re driven by technical curiosity, deep discussions around technology application, broad views of application and system architecture, the latest innovations, and tchotchkes.
2. The business function leaders, sales, and alliance folks who are there to discuss business opportunities, develop leads, establish go-to-market relationships, and close deals. They will be mostly present in side connections in the hallways, ad-hoc discussions at cafes, scheduled meetings in restaurants, the Executive Briefing Center, and in hotel suites (many won’t attend any sessions at all). They’re driven by discussions on solving business problems, networking to expand reach and impact, negotiations on potential deals, and tchotchkes.


Yes, this is a generalization … but overall, you’ll see this dichotomy play out at the event. I’ve recommended that AWS hold an event where there are only side meetings and no sessions to appeal to the latter group – but they have yet to take me up on it. If they ever do, I take full credit 😊


This is important to know, as you should shape your expectations and plans based on the audience you are targeting. If you intend to engage with the technical attendees, focus on the sessions and the Expo – have your best technologists prepared for the right discussions and demonstrate as much hands-on innovation as possible. This audience wants to stay close to the center of the technical content and sessions – so try not to pull them away from the core conference locations.


On the other hand, if you’re targeting the business side, you’ll have more luck in the hallways, meeting rooms, restaurants, outside events, and briefing centers. They’re not as committed to the formal event content and technical sessions, so don’t mind straying from the Venetian/Palazzo home base – provided it’s worth their time.


It seems logical … but I’ve seen some organizations put effort and investment that isn’t specific to the audience they’re targeting – ending up with suboptimal results. This is best addressed in early planning, but certainly is worth considering while there.


Of course, the one consistent consideration: Always have tchotchkes.


Look for me at **Booth #1392** . Stop by to see Pega Blueprint in action, talk about how AI can help[modernize legacy systems](https://www.pega.com/legacy-modernization) , or just compare notes on surviving another week of re:Invent. Looking forward to seeing everyone in Vegas! - Dan


(the fact that I’m low on branded socks and external phone chargers has absolutely nothing to do with my guidance 😊)
